BiblicalUsage: Galuth is the captivity, and concretely the exiles themselves. Daniel is called a man of the captives of Judah in Daniel 2:25, and the king asks whether he is that Daniel, which is of the children of the captivity of Judah, in Daniel 5:13. The same Daniel is accused as one of the children of the captivity in Daniel 6:13, and after the return the children of the captivity kept the dedication of the house of God with joy in Ezra 6:16.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the captivity is the long shadow over Daniel's whole life, and the joy of the return is its sunrise. Daniel stayed faithful in exile, and the exiles came home to dedicate the house. I hold that God keeps His people in captivity and brings them home in joy.
